package_info.why_malicious: The package contains an init.ps1 script that is automatically executed upon installation, which launches a browser in incognito mode to a cryptocurrency price page and repeatedly spawns pop-up messages. This demonstrates abuse of NuGet's auto-executing script feature, which can be leveraged for more harmful attacks.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Start-Process 'chrome.exe' -ArgumentList '--incognito https://www.coindesk.com/price/bitcoin'
while ($true) { [System.Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show('You have been hacked! Trick or Treat') }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the script launches Chrome in incognito mode to display the Bitcoin price page, then enters an infinite loop displaying pop-up messages with 'You have been hacked! Trick or Treat', resulting in user disruption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script executes automatically during package installation, launches a web browser without user consent, and creates an infinite loop of pop-up messages, which is disruptive and indicative of abuse.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal NuGet packages should not execute arbitrary scripts or spawn browsers/pop-ups during installation. This behavior is unexpected and can be leveraged for more serious attacks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may use install scripts for environment setup, but not for launching browsers or displaying prank pop-ups.
key_indicators: Presence of init.ps1 with executable code
No user interaction required to trigger behavior

attack_chain.action: Upon package installation, the init.ps1 script is automatically executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Browser is launched and pop-up messages are displayed to the user.

attack_chain.action: The script launches Chrome in incognito mode to a cryptocurrency price page.
attack_chain.leads_to: User's browser is opened without consent.

attack_chain.action: The script enters an infinite loop, displaying prank pop-up messages.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is disrupted by repeated pop-ups; potential for more harmful payloads in similar attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of init.ps1 with process execution commands
Automatic browser launch during NuGet package installation
Infinite or repeated pop-up message creation in install scripts
file_indicators: init.ps1 containing Start-Process or MessageBox calls
network_indicators: Opening external URLs (e.g., coindesk.com) via browser from install scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan NuGet packages for the presence of init.ps1 scripts. Analyze the script content for process execution commands (e.g., Start-Process) and UI manipulation (e.g., MessageBox). Flag packages that attempt to launch browsers or create pop-ups during installation, as these are strong indicators of abuse or prank/malicious behavior.
